planting.note: Sow indoors mid-September through mid-October, 6-8 weeks before transplanting; transplant into the garden in late fall to overwinter for an early bulb harvest.

directions: Vidora is a new-for-2026 short-day F1 onion from Johnny's Selected Seeds bred for early, highly bolt-resistant bulbing, producing uniform globe-shaped bulbs with a classic sweet Granex flavor. It carries intermediate resistance to pink root and stores up to about three months under good conditions, reaching maturity roughly 130 days from fall planting. Start seed indoors in trays in mid-September through mid-October and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil with a pH of 6.0-7.0. Space plants 1.5-2 inches apart for maximum yield of smaller bulbs, or 3-4 inches apart for larger onions.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-7 weeks before transplanting; move outside after all frost danger has passed and soil has warmed.

directions: Marmango is one of Johnny's new-for-2026 F1 tomato introductions, bred to pair heirloom-like flavor and appearance with modern productivity and disease tolerance. Small 5-8 ounce ribbed beefsteak fruits develop vivid orange color inside and out early in ripening, giving growers a wide harvest window across several maturity stages. The indeterminate vines stay vigorous through an extended production cycle and perform as a greenhouse or tunnel crop as well as in the open field. Trellis and prune to a single or double leader, allowing 4-6 square feet of growing area per leader.

common_name: Unity Tomato (Organic Early Red Beefsteak F1)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-7 weeks before transplanting; supplemental lighting recommended for greenhouse/tunnel production.

directions: Unity is a new-for-2026 organic F1 beefsteak tomato bred by Dr. Kevin Cook at Johnny's Selected Seeds in collaboration with NCSU, built for high-performing early production in field and tunnel. Fruit is attractive with a light green shoulder, weighing 8-12 ounces with few defects and a mild, pleasing flavor typical of the beefsteak class. The compact, generative indeterminate plants are easier to train than average and come into production early, backed by a disease resistance package covering Fusarium wilt, late blight, nematodes, leaf molds, and verticillium wilt. Allow 4-6 square feet of growing area per leader when trellising and pruning for tunnel or greenhouse culture.

planting.note: Direct seed once soil has reached at least 55-60F (treated seed) or 65F (untreated); plant in blocks of at least 4 rows for pollination.

directions: Ultra Violet is a new-for-2026 sh2 super-sweet corn from Johnny's Selected Seeds, prized for 8-inch ears with 14-20 rows of multicolored pink, purple, and white kernels that hold their vivid color through boiling, blanching, or grilling. Plants grow tall, 6-12 feet, with deep purple stalk coloration, strong husk protection, and excellent row fill even late in the sh2 maturity window of about 80 days. Direct seed 3/4-1 inch deep and 6-9 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart, thinning as needed, and plant in blocks rather than single rows to ensure full pollination. Give it full sun and consistent moisture through tasseling and ear fill.

common_name: Doron Prospera Active DMR Basil (Glossy Purple Downy-Mildew-Resistant Basil)

planting.note: Direct seed after frost danger passes, or start indoors 6 weeks before transplanting.

directions: Doron Prospera Active DMR is a new-for-2026 organic purple basil from Johnny's Selected Seeds bred for enhanced downy mildew resistance beyond earlier Prospera releases, along with glossier leaves and a fuller plant habit. Its 3-4 inch glossy, cupped, dark purple-red leaves carry the traditional Genovese basil aroma and reach harvest in about 74 days. Direct seed a quarter-inch deep at 2-3 seeds per inch in rows 18 inches apart, or start indoors 6 weeks before transplanting, thinning to a final spacing of 4-8 inches. Grow in full sun with consistently moist, moderately rich soil, since the plant is prone to heat stress and offers little drought tolerance.

common_name: Antibes Apricot I Snapdragon (Cool-Season F1 Cut-Flower Snapdragon)

planting.note: Surface-sow indoors 8-10 weeks before transplanting; grow as a cool-season crop since it is not recommended for summer flowering.

directions: Antibes Apricot I is a new-for-2026 Group 1 F1 snapdragon from Johnny's Selected Seeds, bred for performance under the short days and low temperatures of cool-season production rather than summer flowering. Its saturated peach-apricot blooms stand out from similar apricot snapdragons that lean more yellow or cream, and the edible, lightly fragrant flowers suit cut-flower bouquets and food garnishes alike. Surface-sow seed indoors 8-10 weeks before transplanting, since light is required for germination, and pinch young plants to encourage branching. Grow stems to 28-36 inches tall in full sun to part shade, transplanting to larger containers once true leaves appear.
